newsitem.title: NORWAY: Record 129 candidates for 1997 Nobel Peace Prize.
newsitem.headline: Record 129 candidates for 1997 Nobel Peace Prize.

text.p: Norway's Nobel Committee said on Tuesday a record 129 nominations had poured in for this year's Nobel Peace Prize.

Geir Lundestad, director of the committee, told the national news agency NTB that 103 individuals and 26 organisations had been put forward as candidates by various legislators, government ministers, former Nobel winners and other eligible nominators.
Nominations are valid if postmarked before February 1.
Lundestad was speaking after the committe held its first meeting to shortlist candidates for the coveted award.
True to its commitment not to reveal the names of Nobel candidates, the committee refuses to confirm any nomination, but Lundestad said many had been nominated before.
However, this year's list is known to include jailed Chinese dissident Wei Jingsheng. Other likely candidates are believed to be former U.S. President Jimmy Carter and the Salvation Army.
The committee will meet five to six times in all before it announces a decision in mid-October.
The 1996 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to two East Timor human rights campaigners -- Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo and self-exiled activist Jose Ramos Horta.
